WHAT: Replaced regex-based bash command classification with shfmt AST parsing to correctly handle compound commands, pipes, subshells, and `&&` chains without false positives.

PROBLEM WITH REGEX: `echo 'git push'` would trigger the risky pattern for `git push` even though the command is just echoing text. Regex can't distinguish running `git push` from the literal string "git push".

SHFMT APPROACH:
- `shfmt --tojson <<< "$cmd"` parses bash into JSON AST
- jq recursively extracts all `CallExpr` nodes to get actual executable names
- Only actual command invocations (not string literals) are checked
- Handles pipes, &&, $(), subshells correctly

IMPLEMENTATION: `/Users/ned/Desktop/Projects/pixel-office/src/lib/tool-classifier.ts` — uses Node `child_process.spawnSync('shfmt', ['--tojson'])` for complex bash, falls back to simple regex for single commands.

REFERENCE: https://github.com/oryband/claude-code-auto-approve — source of this approach
